T-2374: the Agency House's two grounded apertures are holes again, not striped ladders (#1690)

* T-2374: the Agency House's front aperture count, from its own picture

The Wau-Bun panorama of 1831 draws Cobweb Castle's front gable with TWO upright
dark marks standing on the ground and ONE small mark above them. The log_dwelling
compound path states ONE opening per room, so that front was not sayable in data
at all, and every data-only trial was correctly refused by the archetype's own
validation; splitting the centre room to get a second opening would change the
roof and the walls the rest of the record states.

`compound_apertures` is the opt-in that says it: an explicit set on ONE room's
outward face, which OVERRIDES that room's singular `front_opening` so the old
centred door cannot survive among the new marks as a phantom — in the mesh or in
the front-wall reading the entrance, apron and signboard generators share. It is
bounded: inside the wall or under the room's own roof rake, clear of its
neighbours, at most one stated way in, refused on the bounded elbow and on a
record with no stated rooms, and absent by default everywhere else.

What the picture gives is the COUNT and roughly the arrangement along the face.
Every coordinate is set out from this record's own 5 m centre wall and its own
rake; the recess section is this archetype's existing opening kit; and the entry
role on the right-hand mark is a design inference, not a reading — it goes there
because that is where the old centre door stood, so the town's one grounded
entrance on that front stays one entrance. No glazing, closure, leaf, shutter,
interior, attic room, white paint or historic function is claimed, and the white
of the engraving's paper is not evidence of paint. L-cobweb-apertures-2374
records all of it.

Built and qualified on the pinned, sha256-verified Blender 4.5.3 on Ubuntu 26.04
in four bounded batches: all 82 log_dwelling masters regenerated, and 81 came out
BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is the measurement that the option is genuinely off for
every other record. Cobweb's master moved
af1f33c0f5d75fc8c40e6cbb589adfd7d29d551572c2775e236bb260f6ee561f (139,824 B) ->
4f42207be5fcb2391fda58672ce8442b02aba9510f3096db8c2934b695fe7bea (139,248 B)
and its web derivative
49cfcb869c0a39bd936c2c22428179538c37c5a380b9f27c53fab019719b8dcd (31,804 B) ->
1699d7aa1c4b0abb6229bd4cbfaed95013f3ede9323f4945396583fd14b26e23 (30,304 B).
No other archetype family, structure version or foreign registry row is touched.

Not a match. The panorama's camera remains UNSOLVED and is not enrolled in
data/reference_views/; the compound's overall width, the wing and sub-roof
silhouettes, the roof junctions and valleys, the text-attested partial
clapboarding and the finish and tone all still differ from the picture; the
source is retrospective 1831 context printed in 1881 and is not proof of the
building as it stood on 1835-07-01. T-2374's image gate stays open.

Gate: tools/check.sh --part 1/4 .. 4/4, all four green (1,150 steps, none red).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-2374: the Agency House's two grounded apertures are holes again, not striped ladders

The first cut of `compound_apertures` put its dark face 0.004 m out from the wall
PLANE, because it passed the bare `APERTURE_BACK_M` to `openings.face`. But
`openings.surround` reads its `back` from the wall's SKIN and ran the reveal to
0.026 m, and a log wall's courses stand 0.022 m proud. So the face sat BEHIND the
logs and both grounded apertures were crossed by horizontal courses — they read as
striped ladders rather than holes. An independent fixed-camera review of the
committed meshes found it; every numeric check, both smoke legs and the application
review had passed, because the fault lived in a depth no reading looks at.

The face is now given `w.skin + APERTURE_BACK_M`, the same absolute offset the
surround's own reveal runs back to. That is the convention `_opening`'s blind
doorway already follows in this file (`back = -0.30 - w.skin` beside
`face(..., -0.30, ...)`), and it is what `APERTURE_BACK_M`'s own comment says the
constant is for: the dark face, just proud of the logs' own relief.

`tools/test_log_compound_apertures.py` now pins the invariant by reading the
builder's source — the surround's `back` and the face's offset must be the same
absolute offset, and that offset must exceed `RELIEF_M`. Reverting the one
expression makes it fail; the guard was checked against the defect both ways.

No shared helper, schema, recipe scheme, camera, grade or match verdict is touched,
and no other record states a set. Rebuilt on pinned sha-verified Blender 4.5.3 on
Ubuntu 26.04.1: all 82 log_dwelling masters in four bounded batches, 81 of them
byte-identical. Cobweb's MASTER 4f42207b -> 1ddf548d, WEB 1699d7aa -> 99997b5f.

T-2374 stays OPEN/PARTIAL: the panorama's camera is still UNSOLVED and unenrolled,
and the compound's width, wings, sub-roofs, roof junctions, partial clapboarding,
finish and tone all still differ from the picture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
